transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO, Zeppelin), Ravi Singh (Lead ML Eng, Zeppelin), Emily Chen (Product, Zeppelin)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Zeppelin's use case for a self-serve PLG flow, evaluate Redwood hosted API for quickstart and discuss potential Dedicated/Private requirements for later POC. Customer cares about time-to-first-token, security (SOC2/KMS), and predictable latency under burst load.

00:00 Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intro - i'm alex, i'm the AE on this account, and with me is samir from our solutions eng team. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Maya Lopez: good, thanks. busy week but excited to chat. we had a few quick goals for this call, mainly understand how fast we can get a POC running with Redwood, what free credits/quickstart looks like, and where Dedicated/Private might fit for us down the line.
00:22 Samir Patel: awesome, that's perfect. quick agenda from our side: 1) understand your current stack and success criteria, 2) show the quickstart flow and time-to-first-token expectations, 3) discuss security/compliance and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and 4) agree next steps. sound good?
00:36 Ravi Singh: yes. i'll jump in with infra questions. we run most things on AWS in us-west-2, heavy use of k8s and some in-house inference for embeddings. currently using OpenAI for a few features but costs are creeping up, and we need better latency at our edge for certain flows.
00:52 Emily Chen: and from product, we want to evaluate how fast we can iterate — free credits for engineers, simple SDKs, and shipping a feature within 2-3 weeks is the target.
01:05 Alex Kim: cool, so two high-level needs: quick time-to-value for product teams via our PLG quickstart, and then a path to Dedicated or Private for production SLA and data controls. can you share current qps and token volume ballpark?
01:16 Ravi Singh: rough numbers: 150qps for embeddings at peak? no, sorry that's wrong — maybe 15 qps for our main API, embeddings batch jobs overnight, tokens maybe 5-10M tokens/month currently for prod features, higher if we flip on more users. latency target is p95 under 300ms for most text generation calls.
01:38 Samir Patel: that's helpful. our hosted API can definitely get you started; PLG quickstart typically gets engineers to first token in under an hour — usually minutes if you follow the quickstart. free credits we provide for initial evals (we'll send a redemption link). for p95 300ms, depends on model choice and sequence length, but we have verified profiles for common open models.
01:58 Maya Lopez: can you clarify the difference between hosted and dedicated? specifically around routing, cost predictability and data isolation.
02:08 Alex Kim: yeah, hosted is our public Redwood API with per-token billing — it's fastest to start and supports streaming, functions, embeddings, everything. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for a customer — you get predictable throughput, capacity isolation, and better tail latency guarantees. Private adds the VPC or on-prem control plane, KMS integrations, and full audit logs for compliance.
02:28 Ravi Singh: and the quickstart — does it require us to share any data? we prefer not to send PII during early evals.
02:34 Samir Patel: no, you can run the quickstart with synthetic or anonymized data. the free account and credits are isolated to your org and you control what you send. we also have per-route retention settings and can enable no-persist mode for sensitive tests.
02:46 Emily Chen: what's time-to-first-token look like for a simple prompt? in our experience, onboarding flows that take more than a day lose momentum.
02:54 Samir Patel: typically first token in <5 minutes if you grab an API key and run curl or the SDK. time-to-first meaningful demo with a sample prompt and UI is usually under an hour — that's with our quickstart repo, prebuilt templates.
03:10 Maya Lopez: good. on the security side we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS for keys, and audit logs. also potential requirement for data residency in eu-west-1 next year.
03:24 Alex Kim: we can share our SOC 2 report and security pack — i'll attach to the follow-up. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. for KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. residents — we have regions in NA and EU, and Private gives you full control over where data lives.
03:42 Ravi Singh: for Dedicated, how does the autoscaling and burst capacity work? we have traffic spikes and want to avoid throttling.
03:50 Samir Patel: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and a burst buffer — you set policy and can use burst credits. if you need absolute guarantees, Dedicated with reserved capacity is best. for hosted we do smart routing and fallbacks, but it's multi-tenant so occasional tail variability could happen.
04:08 Maya Lopez: pricing is always a touchy subject — how do we estimate cost savings versus OpenAI?
04:15 Alex Kim: depends heavily on model and quantization. our Optimize toolkit gives model and quantization recommendations by workload; many customers see 30-60% cost improvement vs comparable hosted providers by using batching, KV cache, and quantized model variants. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet as well.
04:31 Ravi Singh: can we run a time-to-first-token benchmark? like we want to measure cold start latency from our app to Redwood hosted vs Dedicated options in us-west-2.
04:39 Samir Patel: absolutely — Samir will prepare a short benchmark plan. typical tests include: simple text-gen at varying seq lengths, embeddings throughput, and cold vs warmed KV cache. we can instrument with tracing hooks.
04:50 Maya Lopez: great. one more question: is there an SDK for our stack? we use Node and Go primarily.
04:57 Alex Kim: yes, official SDKs for Node, Python; community Go SDKs and we can share best-practice snippets. our quickstart repo has a Node example that wires up streaming responses and a simple UI.
05:12 Emily Chen: any friction in getting free credits for engineers? we need to distribute quickly to a small eng team.
05:18 Alex Kim: not at all — i'll send a redemption link and step-by-step. usually you create org, redeem credits, and developers can immediately generate API keys.
05:25 Ravi Singh: what about auditability during the POC? we want logs of requests and ability to disable persistence if needed.
05:31 Samir Patel: retention controls and audit logging available; no-persist mode can be enabled for accounts. we'll include details in the security doc.
05:42 Maya Lopez: sounds good. on timeline: if we get credits and a quickstart up, we'd like to have a working demo by 2026-06-10 and a POC with infra benchmarks prior to June 25.
05:54 Alex Kim: noted — that's doable. i'll follow up with the quickstart link and SOC2/security pack by 2026-06-03. samir will share the bench plan by 2026-06-05.
06:04 Ravi Singh: for Dedicated/Private cost estimation, can we get rough pricing ranges upfront so we can budget?
06:09 Alex Kim: yes, i'll include high-level Dedicated pricing and the variables that affect it (reserved GPU sizes, commitment term, burst capacity). detailed quote requires rough throughput numbers which you can share.
06:20 Maya Lopez: ok, let's recap next steps.
06:22 Alex Kim: recap: 1) Alex send quickstart guide + credit link + security pack (SOC2/KMS docs) by 6/3. 2) Ravi to share sample dataset and target latencies by 6/4. 3) Samir to send short benchmark plan for time-to-first-token and p95 tests by 6/5. 4) schedule infra deep-dive with Ravi week of 6/8. any other items?
06:40 Emily Chen: we'll look at the quickstart and try to get to first token this week.
06:45 Maya Lopez: thank you, appreciate the clarity.
06:48 Alex Kim: thanks everyone. we'll send notes and links after.

Links/shared artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood quickstart repo (link shared in follow-up)
- Security pack and SOC2 (to be attached)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (to be shared)

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors in proper nouns (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate'), and timestamps approximate.

End of call.
